thread:
olivia: FYI we got a support ticket from a customer (no PII pasted) saying their assistant responses started including weird hesitation markers and trailing ellipses after the v9.2 rollout.
olivia: Customer examples pasted in email:
---
User prompt: "Summarize the onboarding steps for our app."
Model v9.1 (before): "Sure — here are the steps: 1) Create an account. 2) Verify email. 3) Complete profile. Let me know if you want templates."
Model v9.2 (after): "Sure — here are the steps... 1) Create an account. 2) Verify email. 3) Complete profile... (let me know if you want templates)"
---
olivia: They say it's subtle but consistent across many examples: added ellipses, parenthetical hedges, shorter sentence tails. They flagged user-facing UX as feeling "hesitant".
sam_support: ack. Do we have customer request IDs or any request_sample_id? We need a request_id to grab traces.
olivia: They sent one request_id: req_2026-03-15_7a9b2c. Also included a screenshot of the raw API response body. Pasting sanitized snippet:
```
{ "id": "resp_xyz",
  "request_id": "req_2026-03-15_7a9b2c",
  "model": "redwood-9.2",
  "output": "Sure — here are the steps... 1) Create an account. 2) Verify email...",
  "decoding": { "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95 }
}
```
eng-aaron: interesting. rolling note: v9.2 was pushed as a canary -> prod last night at 02:18 UTC. ops-bot should have the deploy timeline.
ops-bot: Deploy log: canary start 2026-03-15T02:05:12Z; canary promote 2026-03-15T02:18:47Z; route traffic incremented to 100% by 02:40Z. Release tag: redwood-9.2+optimize-kernel.
eng-lee: quick hypothesis: the model's new fine-tune or decoding tweaks could be adding punctuation patterns. Could also be beam/stop-token changes. We should reproduce with same model and decoding params.
eng-aaron: steps to repro I recommend:
  1) Use model redwood-9.2 with the same decoding settings (temp 0.2, top_p 0.95) and the original system+user prompt. Use the exact tokenization (detokenize the customer's logged input).
  2) Try same prompt against redwood-9.1 and compare diffs (string diff + punctuation stats).
  3) Run 100-sample batch with slight temp variations (0.0, 0.2, 0.5) and record frequency of ellipses, parentheses, trailing "...", and short parenthetical notes.
sam_support: I can run the 1-off quick check with the customer prompt. Do we want a temporary rollback or a canary split? Customer is upset but not P0.
eng-lee: before rollback let's check if it's decoder-config-only: run v9.2 with temperature=0.0 and deterministic sampling. If ellipses disappear, we can surface config change to customers and/or patch default config.
eng-aaron: also check recent fine-tune diff: dataset included some chat transcripts with 'hesitation' markers from human transcripts? I'll diff the FT dataset commit between v9.1 -> v9.2: ref ft/datasets/seq_x commit f4c3.
olivia: I ran a quick local test (same prompt + temp 0.2) and reproduced the trailing ellipses on two runs. I also tried temp 0.0 and it still produced one "..." in one run.
eng-lee: hmm so not purely sampling. Could be a tokenization or splice inserted during preproc/postproc. Check post-render hooks that add parentheses for suggestions.
eng-aaron: can someone pull the model output hooks logs for resp_xyz? If it's postproc, we'd see it in the render trace: trace/render/resp_xyz.log
sam_support: grabbing logs now — attaching curated lines:
```
[render] model_out_tokens: ["Sure", " — ", "here", "are", "the", "steps", "...", "1", ")", ...]
[postproc] detection: trailing_ellipsis_normalizer -> applied
```
sam_support: looks like there's a postproc normalizer that was enabled in 9.2 to handle trailing pauses; it seems to inject ellipses when it detects certain token sequences.
eng-lee: that aligns. The normalizer was added to compress "pause" tokens into visible ellipses for accessibility tests. Looks like it slipped into prod without an opt-out flag.
eng-aaron: immediate plan:
 - eng-lee: open rollback PR to disable normalizer or add opt-in flag for now. Tag: hotfix/disable-ellipsis-normalizer
 - operations: hold rollback until we confirm impact scope (how many customers affected). If large, perform targeted rollback for support customers.
 - sam_support: reply to customer acknowledging receipt, provide repro plan and ETA 24h.
olivia: I'll send the customer the acknowledgement and ask for a few more sample prompts to help quantify.
eng-lee: I'll revert the normalizer locally and run CI tests, then push hotfix to canary. If results look good, promote.
eng-aaron: add a short eval that counts punctuation anomalies across the public regression suite and run before/after.
sam_support: thanks all. tagging @eng-aaron @eng-lee. I'll log this thread into the customer ticket and mark as "investigating".
olivia: thanks team. Next update in ~2–3 hours once canary hotfix lands. :hourglass:
